what: Roof area, squares, shingle bundles and underlayment
title: Roofing Calculator: How Many Bundles of Shingles Do I Need? | Calcupine
description: Estimate roof area from your house size and pitch, then get squares, shingle bundles, underlayment, nails and drip edge. Free roofing calculator.
lede: Enter the house length and width, the overhang and the roof pitch. The calculator works out the real roof area and the shingles, underlayment and nails to order.

faq.a: 100 square feet of roof. A 1,500 sq ft roof is 15 squares.

faq.q: How many bundles of shingles are in a square?
faq.a: Three bundles per square is standard for three-tab and most architectural shingles. Some heavier designer shingles use four or five; check the wrapper.

faq.q: How do I find my roof pitch?
faq.a: Pitch is how many inches the roof rises for every 12 inches across. Hold a level horizontally against the roof underside or rafter, measure 12 inches along it, and measure straight up to the roof. A 6 inch rise is a 6/12 pitch.

faq.q: How much waste should I add for roofing?
faq.a: About 10% for a simple gable roof and 15% for hip roofs or roofs with valleys and dormers, which need more cutting.

faq.q: How many nails per square of shingles?
faq.a: About 320 for three-tab shingles: 80 shingles per square with 4 nails each. High-wind areas often require 6 nails per shingle (480 per square).
